title: A parameter with the default VAL mode is evaluated before the call, so CALCULATE in the body does not change it
query: DEFINE FUNCTION ComputeForRed = ( amount ) => CALCULATE ( amount, Product[Color] = "Red" )

source.quote: Despite the function body evaluating the parameter in a filter context that filters only red products, the result is the Sales Amount for all the visible product colors.
source.supports: the article gives this function and says the result is the amount of all colors

source.quote: A value parameter is like a variable definition: the formula used by the caller produces a value; this value is assigned to a variable, and then the function is executed.
source.supports: a VAL parameter is evaluated once by the caller, like a variable

derivation: amount has no mode, so it is VAL: [Sales Amount] is evaluated by the caller with no filter, 540. Inside CALCULATE the parameter is that value: 540, not the Red amount 460.
